name: The Detail That Should Not Be There
summary: A disturbance is discovered — a body on a floor, a theft, a disappearance, a ledger that does not balance — and among the ordinary facts sits one small physical thing that no innocent account explains: a second cup washed and back on its hook, a key on the wrong side of a door, a coat too dry for the weather. That single wrongness is what converts a misfortune into a question, and the question is what the investigation is actually about.

beats.label: The disturbance is found
beats.intent: something is discovered that has an obvious innocent reading

beats.label: One detail refuses to fit
beats.intent: a single fact cannot be explained by the innocent reading

beats.label: The question is fixed
beats.intent: the wrongness is stated precisely enough to be pursued

beats.label: The investigation opens
beats.intent: someone commits to answering it against the preference for closure

preconditions.text: an event with a readily available innocent explanation

effects.text: a specific unanswered question now governs what follows
at least one party would prefer the question not be asked

examples.text: Everything in the room said he had been drinking alone; only the second cup, washed and dry and back on its hook, disagreed.

name: The Lead That Fits Too Well
summary: A suspect emerges whom the evidence fits cleanly — the letters are in the one drawer that was searched first, the debts are on record, the alibi is thin — and the investigation commits to that fit publicly, expensively, or emotionally. It collapses not from new evidence but from noticing the fit was too clean: someone arranged for these documents to be found in this order, and that someone is the actual subject.

roles.label: the too-convenient suspect
constraints: is genuinely implicated by the facts

roles.label: whoever arranged the fit
constraints: stays offstage while the lead runs

beats.label: A clean suspect emerges
beats.intent: evidence converges on one person with unusual tidiness

beats.label: The investigation commits
beats.intent: resources, reputation or feeling are staked on the lead

beats.label: The fit is too clean
beats.intent: a seam shows where the evidence was arranged rather than left

beats.label: The lead collapses upward
beats.intent: the false trail becomes the strongest evidence about who laid it

preconditions.text: an investigation under pressure to produce a name

effects.text: the investigator has lost standing and must proceed with less
the existence of a deliberate arranger is now established

examples.text: Every document they needed was in the one drawer they searched first, which was exactly what finally bothered her about it.

name: It Could Not Have Happened
summary: The crime is bounded by constraints that make it impossible — a room bolted from the inside, a stair watched all night, an alibi sworn to by strangers, a distance no one could ride in the hours available. The constraints are enumerated honestly, one by one, and the answer comes from finding the one that was never a checked fact at all but an assumption everybody in the house shared.

roles.label: the one enumerating constraints
constraints: must state them honestly to break them

roles.label: the impossibility
constraints: holds until one item is reclassified

beats.label: The impossibility is stated
beats.intent: the crime is shown to be excluded by the known constraints

beats.label: The constraints are listed
beats.intent: each condition is set out so it can be tested rather than felt

beats.label: One is only an assumption
beats.intent: a constraint is found that no one ever actually checked

beats.label: The impossibility dissolves
beats.intent: with the assumption removed the sequence becomes ordinary

preconditions.text: a set of conditions treated as facts by everyone present

effects.text: the method is now known even if the hand is not
who benefited from the shared assumption is a new question

examples.text: Four people swore the door was watched all night, and every one of them was telling the truth about a different night.

name: The Witness Whose Lie Is Not the Crime
summary: A statement is given that contradicts one small checkable thing — the hour on a receipt, which train was running, whose window faces the yard — and pressing the contradiction produces not a confession to the crime but a confession to something else entirely: a debt, an affair, a night spent at a hospital they will not name. The lie is real, the reason is unrelated, and that unrelated reason is what unlocks the case.

roles.label: the lying witness
constraints: is lying about something, but not this

roles.label: the unrelated secret
constraints: is shameful enough to lie for

beats.label: The account is given
beats.intent: a witness supplies an account that is mostly consistent

beats.label: A small fact contradicts it
beats.intent: a checkable detail does not match the account

beats.label: The lie is pressed
beats.intent: the contradiction is put to the witness directly

beats.label: The reason is the find
beats.intent: the witness confesses to something unrelated that reframes the case

preconditions.text: a witness with something to lose that is not the crime

effects.text: the case file holds a new established fact — a hidden relationship — set beside nothing yet
the witness's timeline is corrected, moving someone else

examples.text: He had not been at the warehouse and he would not say where he had been, and it took two more days to learn it was a hospital.

name: The Investigation Provokes a Second
summary: The asking of questions makes someone dangerous to somebody, and a second body follows — characteristically the person who had agreed to talk in the morning and was found before the morning came. The interview that never happened says more than the answer would have: only those who knew what was about to be said could have moved, the field narrows to them, and the investigator now carries a death their own questions provoked.

roles.label: the one whose questions provoked it
the second victim
constraints: was about to say something useful

roles.label: whoever moved to silence
constraints: must have known what was coming

beats.label: The questions land close
beats.intent: an inquiry reaches someone who now becomes a liability

beats.label: The witness is silenced
beats.intent: the person about to speak is removed

beats.label: The field narrows
beats.intent: only those who knew what was coming could have acted

beats.label: The investigator carries it
beats.intent: responsibility for provoking the death changes how they proceed

preconditions.text: an inquiry that has become visible to its subject

effects.text: the case file now holds established facts about who had foreknowledge, still unconnected to each other
the suspect pool is reduced to those who knew what the dead witness was about to say
the investigator now has a personal stake they did not choose

examples.text: She had asked him to come in the morning; he was found before the morning, which told her more than his answer would have.

name: Two Facts, One Origin
summary: Two things that have sat in the case file as unrelated — two names, two dates, a sum in a ledger and a village in a letter — turn out to share one origin, and the shape of the case redraws itself around it. Nothing new is found; a fact already in hand simply becomes the centre, and people who had been cleared are back in scope.

beats.label: Two facts sit unrelated
beats.intent: both are known and neither is connected to the other

beats.label: A shared origin appears
beats.intent: something incidental reveals they come from one place

beats.label: The case redraws
beats.intent: the known facts rearrange around the new centre

preconditions.text: a case file that holds established facts which have never been set beside each other

effects.text: the centre of the case has moved without new evidence
previously dismissed parties are back in scope

examples.text: The bank in the ledger and the village in the letter turned out to be a hundred paces apart, and everything else rearranged itself around that.

name: The Chain Laid Out
summary: The household is gathered in one room and the sequence is walked through in front of all of them, step by step, each step resting only on things already shown — the timetable, the ledger, who could have known the hour. The denial comes, as it must, and is answered by the one item that needs no interpretation, after which what remains is not the question of guilt but the question of what is now done about it.

roles.label: the one laying it out
constraints: uses only what has been shown

roles.label: the assembled parties
constraints: each had a plausible reason to be suspected

beats.label: The parties are gathered
beats.intent: everyone with a stake is put in one room

beats.label: The chain is laid out
beats.intent: the sequence is walked through using only shown facts

beats.label: The denial
beats.intent: the named party refuses and offers the strongest counter

beats.label: The proof that cannot be argued
beats.intent: one item lands that requires no interpretation

beats.label: What follows is consequence
beats.intent: the question turns from guilt to what is now done about it

preconditions.text: enough established facts to build a chain without new evidence

effects.text: the cost of the reveal falls on people who were not guilty

examples.text: He walked them through it twice, and the second time he stopped at the part where only one person in the room could have known the hour.

name: The Investigator Has a Stake
summary: The one asking the questions turns out to be inside the case — related to a party, owed money by one, or the reason the thing happened at all — and did not say so. Judgement bends before anyone notices it bending, and once the connection surfaces every conclusion already entered in the file must be re-earned in front of people who now have grounds to doubt all of it.

beats.label: The stake exists unseen
beats.intent: the investigator is connected to the case without acknowledging it

beats.label: Judgement bends
beats.intent: a decision is made that the stake explains better than the evidence does

beats.label: The connection surfaces
beats.intent: the stake becomes known to the others

beats.label: Everything must be re-earned
beats.intent: prior conclusions must be re-proved to a doubting audience

preconditions.text: an investigator with a prior connection to a party in the case

effects.text: prior conclusions carry no authority until re-proved
the investigator's continued involvement is itself contested

examples.text: It was not that he lied about knowing the family; it was that nobody had thought to ask, and he had let that stand for three weeks.
